as_written_in_papers.quote: A novel variant, c.728T > C, was found, causing an exchange of leucine to proline at residue 243.
| 36 | c.728T > C | p.Leu243Pro | NAD^+ binding domain | 0 | 0.999 | 0.931 | This report |

Here, we present a patient with a severe phenotype of SSADHD caused by a novel genetic variant c.728T > C that leads to an exchange of leucine to proline at residue 243, located within the highly conserved nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD)^+ binding domain of SSADH.

cases.statement: One person: a 23-year-old woman with SSADH deficiency confirmed biochemically and by absent lymphocyte enzyme activity, carrying c.728T > C (p.Leu243Pro) with c.278G > T (p.Cys93Phe), described by the authors as compound heterozygosity.

people.label: patient
people.zygosity_or_genotype: compound heterozygous (as stated by the authors; parental genotypes not reported)
people.key_phenotypes: developmental delay from 4 months; truncal hypotonia; elevated urinary and CSF GHB with absent lymphocyte SSADH activity; therapy-resistant focal and bilateral seizures from age 6; autism spectrum disorder

quotes.quote: The female patient described herein was born at term to non-consanguineous parents after an uneventful pregnancy.
After an inconspicuous newborn period, developmental delay was noted at 4 months of age due to the absence of grasping.
During infancy, the main clinical findings were truncal hypotonia and diurnal changes of the vigilance.
Levels of GABA and GHB in the CSF were also elevated, whereas SSADH enzymatic activity in lymphocytes was absent.
The epilepsy was therapy-resistant with the assumed side-effects to lamotrigine, oxcarbamazepine, levetiracetam (also in combination), and a short valproate trial.
The patient, now aged 23 years, suffers from an autism spectrum disorder with repetitive movements, anxiety, and social withdrawal, characteristic for SSADH deficient patients.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Elevated GHB in urine and CSF with absent SSADH activity in lymphocytes; the authors call the features typical for SSADHD. No other genes were reported as tested (Sanger sequencing of ALDH5A1 only).

quotes.quote: Semi-quantitative analysis of organic acids in the urine revealed increased levels of GHB and γ-butyrolacton.
Levels of GABA and GHB in the CSF were also elevated, whereas SSADH enzymatic activity in lymphocytes was absent.
A confirmation of the diagnosis was achieved by a complete absence of SSADH enzyme activity in lymphocytes.
Here, we present the case of a 23-year-old female patient with severe developmental abnormalities and behavioral changes typical for SSADHD.
Focal and secondary bilateral seizures with and without loss of consciousness started at the age of six years.

segregation.statement: Not reported for the variant. The family history is given without genotypes: the father has recurrent seizures not further evaluated, a paternal uncle has autism spectrum disorder, and one brother is healthy; none were reported as tested.

quotes.quote: The family history of the patient’s mother was unremarkable; whereas the patient’s father suffers from recurrent seizures that have not been further evaluated.
The paternal uncle of the patient suffers from an autism spectrum disorder that has not been further investigated.
The patient has one healthy brother.

in_trans.statement: Other allele c.278G > T (p.Cys93Phe). The authors state compound heterozygosity, but only a patient sample is described as sequenced; parental genotypes are not reported (consent was obtained from both parents).

quotes.quote: Analysis of the ALDH5A1 gene showed heterozygosity for a known missense variant, c.278G > T, leading to a replacement of cysteine to phenylalanine at residue 93 and resulting in a reduced activity of the SSADH enzyme to about 3% when expressed in vitro [12].
The sequencing of the ALDH5A1 gene revealed compound heterozygosity for a known pathogenic variant as well as a novel variant.
Genomic DNA was isolated from a patient blood sample using standard procedures.
For genetic analysis, written informed consent was obtained from the patient and both parents.

functional.statement: Two assays. (1) Patient dermal fibroblasts (carrying both variants): ALDH5A1 mRNA similar to two controls, SSADH protein nearly absent on Western blot; the two controls themselves differed in protein level. (2) p.Leu243Pro construct in CRISPR SSADH-knockout HEK293T cells versus wild-type construct: no protein and 0.7% of wild-type activity (three independent experiments).

quotes.quote: We used patient-derived dermal fibroblasts to assess the mRNA expression of ALDH5A1 and found no difference compared to two independent non-SSADHD control subjects (Figure 2A).
However, Western blot analysis revealed a nearly complete absence of SSADH protein expression in patient fibroblasts compared to two independent non-SSADHD control samples.
Interestingly, the non-SSADHD samples also revealed substantial differences in the expression patterns of the SSADH protein (Figure 2B).
Upon transfection of a plasmid carrying the wildtype cDNA into the knockout line, SSADH expression increases, whereas transfection of the mutant construct shows no protein expression.
After transfection of the SSADH knockout cell line with the mutant construct, an enzyme activity of only 0.7% of the wildtype could be detected (Figure 2C,D).
Data are expressed as mean ± SD of three independent experiments.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense substitution p.(Leu243Pro) in the region the paper assigns to the NAD+ binding domain. The paper states that ALDH5A1 variants cause loss of function and that the effect of the substitution is protein destabilization.

quotes.quote: Variants of the ALDH5A1 gene (6p22.3, GRCh38.p13: 24,494,969–24,537,207) are known to cause a loss of function of the mitochondrial succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase (SSADH) and were identified in 1981 to be the underlying cause of SSADHD [1].

Thus, in agreement with the results from the in silico stability analysis, the effect of the substitutions is protein destabilization rather than a direct effect on the ability of the protein to bind the cofactor.

Here, we present a patient with a severe phenotype of SSADHD caused by a novel genetic variant c.728T > C that leads to an exchange of leucine to proline at residue 243, located within the highly conserved nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD)^+ binding domain of SSADH.

computational_predictions.statement: Table 2: SIFT 0, PolyPhen 0.999, REVEL 0.931. FoldX monomer ddG 7.63 kcal/mol and homotetramer about 29.36 kcal/mol (destabilizing). Leu243 conserved in 30 mammalian sequences (data not shown).

quotes.quote: | 36 | c.728T > C | p.Leu243Pro | NAD^+ binding domain | 0 | 0.999 | 0.931 | This report |

In silico analyses revealed deleterious effects of the p.Leu243Pro residue replacement, as the calculation of several established pathogenicity scores showed exclusively high values and high probability of destabilizing or deleterious effects on the protein (SIFT score of 0.0 and REVEL score of 0.931).
The monomers of the p.Cys93Phe and p.Le243Pro variants possess a moderate to high destabilizing ΔΔG of 7.20 and 7.63 kcal/mol, respectively.

The tetrameric SSADH protein consisting exclusively of the p.Cys93Phe missense variant monomers revealed a ΔΔG of 28.09 kcal/mol, meaning it has a destabilizing effect on the wildtype structure, while tetramers of p.Leu243Pro showed even higher values at around 29.36 kcal/mol.
An analysis of the sequence homology showed that leucine at position 243 is conserved in all of the 30 mammalian SSADH sequences closest to the human one (data not shown).

authors_classification.statement: The authors call the variant novel and give their own classification in the title and text.

quotes.quote: Title: Succinic Semialdehyde Dehydrogenase Deficiency: In Vitro and In Silico Characterization of a Novel Pathogenic Missense Variant and Analysis of the Mutational Spectrum of ALDH5A1
In summary, we here present an analysis of the mutational spectrum of the ALDH5A1 gene and the functional characterization of a previously unknown variant that is causative for SSADHD.
Both variants are situated within the highly conserved NAD^+ binding domain and independently cause a complete loss of enzyme activity.

concerns: Phase is asserted, not shown: only the patient sample is described as sequenced, and no parental genotypes are reported.
The father has recurrent seizures that were not evaluated and his genotype is not reported; this may matter for interpreting the family history.
The fibroblast result reflects both alleles together (c.278G > T and c.728T > C) and cannot be assigned to this variant alone; the controls themselves varied in SSADH protein level.
A typo in the paper writes "p.Le243Pro" once for p.Leu243Pro.
notes_for_panel: Transcript NM_001080.3 / NP_001071.1 stated by the authors. The other allele c.278G > T is described by the authors as known, with about 3% activity in vitro (citing ref. 12).
